what_changed.summary: Germany lifts operating earnings, but derivative gains, minority ownership and the full cost of growth keep the cash test unfinished.

items.title: Germany now drives most incremental revenue.
items.detail: Remexian contributes C$38.23 M of the C$49.13 M year-on-year sales increase; legacy bricks-and-mortar segment revenue rises 7.3%.

items.title: Operating improvement survives the accounting clean-up.
items.detail: C$8.71 M operating income is up 133%, but the C$12.75 M net-income headline includes a C$11.79 M derivative gain offset by a C$1.29 M contract-asset loss.

items.title: Cash is positive, with a narrower definition than total reinvestment.
items.detail: C$7.02 M company FCF deducts sustaining capital and leases; replacing sustaining capital with all PPE and intangible purchases leaves C$5.61 M.

items.title: The balance-sheet and ownership bridge matters.
items.detail: Restricted cash, cash-settled financing, nonrecourse factoring and Remexian’s 49% minority share all affect the interpretation of consolidated results.

items.title: Price already requires continued progress.
items.detail: Three valuation routes span roughly USD2.39–2.74. The USD2.60 base case assumes stronger recurring owner cash flow, while current controls remain ineffective.

packets.title: KBH: Backlog Grew. Demand per Community Did Not.
packets.page_title: KBH Q3 FY2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: KB Home beat depressed EPS expectations, but lower order absorption and rising net debt temper the apparent discount to book value.

what_changed.summary: KB Home beat depressed EPS expectations, but lower order absorption and rising net debt temper the apparent discount to book value.

items.title: The EPS beat is not a sales rebound.
items.detail: $1.05 EPS exceeded FMP consensus, but revenue fell 19.96% and net income fell 40.56%.

items.title: Backlog rose while selling productivity fell.
items.detail: Backlog grew 1.50% YoY, but orders per community declined from 3.8 to 3.1.

items.title: Built to Order helped sequential margins.
items.detail: Nearly three-quarters of deliveries were BTO; reported housing margin recovered to 16.5% from 15.2%.

items.title: Tax and investment items supported profit.
items.detail: The quarter included a $3.5M gain and a 19.6% effective tax rate versus 23.3% last year.

items.title: The book discount carries inventory and funding risk.
items.detail: Inventory reached $5.981B and defined net debt rose $485.764M from fiscal year-end.

packets.title: LEN: Land-Light, Cash-Heavy
packets.page_title: LEN Q3 FY2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Lennar is building faster with fewer owned lots, but inventory, land deposits and borrowing show why a cheaper-looking balance sheet still needs a cash recovery.

what_changed.summary: Lennar is building faster with fewer owned lots, but inventory, land deposits and borrowing show why a cheaper-looking balance sheet still needs a cash recovery.

items.title: Land-light still ties up cash.
items.detail: Homebuilding cash fell to $1.150 billion while owned inventory and land deposits rose; fewer owned homesites are only one part of capital employed.

items.title: Efficiency improved faster than demand.
items.detail: Cycle time fell to 116 days and construction cost per square foot fell 6% year over year, while new orders declined 9%.

items.title: The volume target moved down.
items.detail: Full-year deliveries are now expected at 80,000–81,000, versus 82,000–83,000 previously; Q4 gross margin guidance is 15.5%–16.0%.

items.title: Small adjusted-EPS gap hides offsetting items.
items.detail: Technology investment losses and a Financial Services benefit pull in opposite directions; $1.23 adjusted EPS does not erase operating pressure.

items.title: Price offers limited cushion.
items.detail: Our $75 base and probability-weighted values sit near a dated $76.74 after-hours trade; High uncertainty calls for a larger margin of safety before BUY.

packets.title: IPHA: Funding Bought Time. The Science Still Has to Pay.
packets.page_title: IPHA H1 2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Sobi closed, new shares arrived and runway extended; a careful cash-and-pipeline valuation explains our HOLD at $1.80 base value.

what_changed.summary: Sobi closed, new shares arrived and runway extended; a careful cash-and-pipeline valuation explains our HOLD at $1.80 base value.

items.title: The transaction closed.
items.detail: Sobi conditions were fulfilled September 16; $75M is triggered, but the release still describes payment as expected.

items.title: The share count changed.
items.detail: August added 17.647M ordinary shares. Disclosed post-placement ordinary shares are 111.719M; our valuation uses 117.822M fully diluted.

items.title: Revenue is not commercial traction.
items.detail: The €3.115M licensing line includes €2.5M from an expired Sanofi option; research financing brings combined income to €5.663M.

items.title: Headline cash has several layers.
items.detail: €21.376M includes €10.480M noncurrent financial assets; separate financial and collaboration obligations also matter.

items.title: The clinical calendar decides the next chapter.
items.detail: PACIFIC-9 is expected in H2 2026; IPH4502 initial data in 2026; TELLOMAK-3 first patient in Q1 2027.

packets.title: LAES: The Cash Cushion Shrinks Per Share
packets.page_title: LAES H1 2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Revenue more than doubled, but cash burn and a larger economic share count weaken the apparent cash bargain at SEALSQ.

what_changed.summary: Revenue more than doubled, but cash burn and a larger economic share count weaken the apparent cash bargain at SEALSQ.

items.title: Revenue recovered faster than costs improved.
items.detail: H1 sales rose 131.1% to $11.151M and gross margin reached 48.5%, yet the operating loss widened to $32.162M. Source: current 6-K financial statements.

items.title: The cash-per-share story changes with the denominator.
items.detail: The filed ordinary count plus five-for-one F-share economics and low-strike options gives 231.141M economic shares. Net liquid assets are $2.08 per share before future spending; the quote capitalization divided by price implies only 142.594M outstanding shares. The separate vendor float field is 113.530M shares, not that outstanding count.

items.title: Cash growth came from financing.
items.detail: H1 operating and investing uses plus currency effects consumed $46.19M before $114.641M of financing inflows. Free cash flow was $-25.249M; the cash balance does not demonstrate operating self-funding.

items.title: Most receivables are related-party balances.
items.detail: Shareholder and other related-party receivables total $16.673M, or 76.8% of total receivables. Customer collection days must therefore use the trade subset, not the headline receivable balance.

items.title: Commercial opportunities still need conversion.
items.detail: Management reaffirmed $27–36M of FY2026 revenue and described more than $225M of potential opportunities through 2029. That pipeline is not contracted backlog; initial post-quantum product revenue remains expected toward late H2 2026.

packets.title: ABVX: The Cash Runway Is Real. So Is the Valuation Risk.
packets.page_title: ABVX Q2 2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Abivax now has funding into Q4 2029 and a planned obefazimod NDA, but nearly $8.6B of diluted value above capital leaves little room for execution mistakes.

what_changed.summary: Abivax now has funding into Q4 2029 and a planned obefazimod NDA, but nearly $8.6B of diluted value above capital leaves little room for execution mistakes.

items.title: Funding risk moved farther out.
items.detail: €402.4M of June liquidity plus €767.1M of July net proceeds supports management’s runway into Q4 2029.

items.title: The denominator moved too.
items.detail: The July offer added 7.36M ADSs; our valuation uses 95.45M diluted ordinary equivalents, not the provider’s stale 73.43M shares.

items.title: The headline loss is partly unusual.
items.detail: A €43.205M royalty-certificate derecognition drove part of Q2’s €117.433M loss, but R&D, G&A and cash burn also rose sharply.

items.title: Regulatory execution is now the center.
items.detail: Management plans an obefazimod UC NDA by year-end 2026 and Crohn’s Phase 2b data in mid-2027.

items.title: Reporting controls remain a risk.
items.detail: The 2025 material weaknesses were not confirmed remediated in the current filing; this packet carries that issue rather than assuming a cure.

packets.title: ANAB: The EPS Is Tax Accounting. The Value Is the Royalty Contract.
packets.page_title: ANAB Q2 2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Anaptys reported growing Jemperli royalties, a one-time tax-driven profit and an unresolved contract case; our HOLD values post-Sagard cash at $58 per share.

what_changed.summary: Anaptys reported growing Jemperli royalties, a one-time tax-driven profit and an unresolved contract case; our HOLD values post-Sagard cash at $58 per share.

items.title: Royalties are growing.
items.detail: H1 Jemperli sales rose 30.3%, pushing Anaptys toward higher contractual tiers.

items.title: The profit headline is misleading.
items.detail: Q2 pretax loss became a large profit only after a $181.491M tax benefit.

items.title: Sagard still gets paid first.
items.detail: About $302.5M had been earned; management estimates paydown in H2 2027.

items.title: The contract is in court.
items.detail: Trial is complete, the October 20 hearing remains ahead and the remedy is unresolved.

items.title: The cash narrative does not reconcile.
items.detail: Audited operating outflows total $52.559M, not the release's $72.9M sentence.

packets.title: Academy Sports (ASO): the tariff cash boost behind the earnings jump
packets.page_title: ASO Q2 FY2026 Research Packet - Charged Alpha
packets.description: ASO Q2 FY2026: verified profit and share-count bridges, tariff refund accounting, cash conversion, three valuation routes and dated signposts.

what_changed.summary: ASO Q2 FY2026: verified profit and share-count bridges, tariff refund accounting, cash conversion, three valuation routes and dated signposts.

items.title: Growth is real, but uneven.
items.detail: Total sales increased 3.0% while comps slipped 0.4%. The store base reached 327 and online sales grew 12.8%. Subtracting comp from total growth is not an exact new-store revenue bridge because the populations and denominators differ.

items.title: Profit did more of the EPS work than the share count.
items.detail: Net income grew 9.94%; diluted shares fell 6.11%. On an old-share-count-first bridge, higher profit adds about $0.18 per share and the lower denominator adds about $0.13. Neither effect should be mistaken for the other.

items.title: The tariff benefit is not a non-GAAP add-back.
items.detail: The $0.06 net EPS benefit remains in reported and adjusted performance. The actual adjusted-income bridge adds equity compensation and a debt-retirement loss, then deducts their tax effects.

items.title: Cash needs a wider lens.
items.detail: H1 operating cash includes tariff refunds, while $72.2M of tariff-claim remittances sits in financing. Reported adjusted FCF is $237.6M; subtracting that financing outflow gives a $165.3M cash illustration, not a measure of recurring FCF.

items.title: The rerating has used much of the valuation cushion.
items.detail: At our approximately $49.99 snapshot, the $50 central value offers almost no upside. The $33/$53/$68 scenarios have a $50 weighted value. A profitable retailer can still be an unattractive fresh purchase when uncertainty is high and the cushion is thin.

packets.title: Baozun (BZUN): the market prices its business at less than zero
packets.page_title: BZUN Q2 2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Baozun (BZUN) Q2 2026 earnings research packet: the call, three valuation routes, scenarios, signposts, earnings quality, balance sheet, risks and catalysts — companion to the Charged Alpha episode.

what_changed.summary: Baozun (BZUN) Q2 2026 earnings research packet: the call, three valuation routes, scenarios, signposts, earnings quality, balance sheet, risks and catalysts — companion to the Charged Alpha episode.

items.title: The operating swing is real but seasonal.
items.detail: Q2 is a mid-size quarter; Q4 (Singles' Day) carries the year. Non-GAAP operating income of RMB74M in Q2 compares with RMB198M in Q4 2025 and RMB8M in Q1 2026 — read the trailing four quarters (RMB269M), not one print.

items.title: Group profit is not shareholder profit.
items.detail: Of RMB43.8M of Q2 net income, RMB26.8M went to minority holders — mostly Cainiao's 37% of the Baotong logistics arm — leaving RMB17.0M for Baozun's shareholders. Any valuation of 'the operating business' has to net this out.

items.title: The cash is the thesis, and it is real:
items.detail: RMB2.81B of cash and short-term investments against RMB1.24B of short-term loans — $231M net, $3.98 per ADS — but it sits inside a Cayman holding structure with minority holders owning 34% of total equity, a small VIE (4.4% of revenue) and a China-ADR discount that has persisted for years.

items.title: Management raised the bar on itself:
items.detail: the 2028 non-GAAP operating income target went from RMB550M (set March 2026) to at least RMB700M (August 2026). Consensus (3–6 analysts) sits at RMB586M for 2028 — the Street does not yet believe it.

items.title: The consumer is the risk, in their own words:
items.detail: E-Commerce product sales fell 9.6% on Home & Furnishing and Cosmetics, and the release says 'soft consumer sentiment'. If that spreads into the services line (63% of revenue), the margin story stalls.

items.title: Operations improved.
items.detail: Gross margin stayed 30.4% while operating profit increased.

items.title: Cash did not keep pace.

items.title: Price requires conversion.

items.title: Minority earnings are not all common earnings.

packets.title: IMPP: Who Owns the Cash Windfall?
packets.page_title: IMPP Q2 2026 Research Packet — Charged Alpha
packets.description: Record freight earnings meet vessel commitments, preferred claims and a changing common-share denominator.

what_changed.summary: Record freight earnings meet vessel commitments, preferred claims and a changing common-share denominator.

items.title: The quarter is strong.
items.detail: More vessels and better freight rates lifted operating profit, despite lower operational utilization.

items.title: The cash screen needs a new denominator.
items.detail: Company shares imply about $264M equity value, above gross cash and deposits.

items.title: Fleet purchases move between cash-flow categories.
items.detail: Seller financing payments make simple investing-only FCF misleading.

items.title: Ownership claims are material.
items.detail: Preferred liquidation priority and the $6.30 warrant pool change per-share value.

items.title: Our discount is a judgment.
items.detail: Related-party incentives and uncertain capital access explain the pre-money haircut; it is not a measured market constant.
